1._section_summary: Abstract describes two studies. Study 1 used a cross-sectional sample of female UK students (n = 215, 17–30 years) and found appearance goals were indirectly, negatively associated with body image via introjected regulation. Study 2 (n = 165, 18–27 years) experimentally manipulated guilt and appearance goals and found guilt increased post-test body anxiety for participants in the guilt condition.

14._section_summary: This brief discussion interprets findings from a single experiment showing that the guilt manipulation produced an indirect effect (via post-test guilt) on body anxiety but no significant direct effect; the effect appears specific to guilt rather than general negative affect. The authors note methodological limitations—guilt and body anxiety were measured at post-test (cross-sectional mediation), pre-test guilt was not measured, and only some participants experienced induced guilt—limiting causal inference and suggesting need for longitudinal and replication work.
